public_rationale: The exact 5.6% share is not established by comparable July records. A dated secondary account estimates four operating buildings, but its IT-load figures cannot simply be divided by an undefined facility-capacity denominator. Earlier reporting also gives a 2027 contract start, creating a material conflict with June 2026. These records warrant withholding endorsement, but do not provide a complete, same-period basis for scoring the combined observation.
limitations: The operating-capacity evidence is estimated and uses inconsistent power definitions.
Contract timing relies on secondary reporting because the underlying agreement was not obtained.
Earlier contract reports and later capacity additions are context rather than decisive July outcome evidence.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Oracle has only 5.6% of the 7.1GW needed for its OpenAI deal, which was meant to begin in June 2026.

statement.excerpt: Oracle is burning its company to the ground to build data centers for OpenAI in pursuit of a $300 billion, five-year-long compute deal that was meant to begin in June 2026 and currently has 5.6% of the 7.1GW of capacity it needs to make that revenue
statement.document_title: The More You Buy, The More You Lose

our_interpretation: The assessed proposition concerns operational Oracle capacity available to OpenAI and the stated contract start. The surrounding financial rhetoric and deal valuation are background, not separate scored propositions.
Currently means the operational state at publication. I use July 1–28, 2026 as the current reporting window, with evidence required to establish the state by July 28.
The numerator and denominator must use the same power definition and cover the same Oracle–OpenAI arrangement.
The stated percentage implies approximately 397.6MW: 7,100MW multiplied by 0.056. This arithmetic is a test threshold, not independent evidence.
A contract beginning in June 2026 does not by itself imply that all contracted capacity was required on that date.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable records establish approximately 5.6% operational capacity on a consistent 7.1GW basis at publication and establish June 2026 as the intended start of the same contract.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish a materially different operational share at publication, a different contracted capacity requirement, or a different intended start date for the same agreement.
